q: A manufacturer has normal capacity of 50000 units and fixed production overheads of Rs 25 lakh. Actual production is 40000 units. Under Ind AS 2, the fixed overhead absorbed into inventory cost is:
o: Rs 25 lakh, since all fixed overheads relate to production
Rs 20 lakh, with Rs 5 lakh expensed as unabsorbed overhead
Rs 31.25 lakh, grossed up to the actual production level
Nil, since fixed production overheads are always period costs
why: Fixed overhead is allocated at the normal capacity rate of Rs 50 per unit, giving Rs 20 lakh on 40000 units, and the unallocated Rs 5 lakh is expensed in the period. Absorbing the full amount would capitalise the cost of idle capacity.

q: A trader holds 1000 units costing Rs 500 each. General selling price is Rs 520 with selling commission of 5 percent of selling price. A firm sales contract exists for 400 of those units at Rs 540. What is the total carrying amount under Ind AS 2?
o: Rs 4,94,000 for the whole holding
why: For the 400 contracted units NRV is 540 less 27 equals 513 which exceeds cost, so they remain at Rs 500 each giving Rs 2,00,000. The other 600 units have NRV of 520 less 26 equals 494, below cost, giving Rs 2,96,400, so the total is Rs 4,96,400.

q: Which of the following is included in the cost of inventories under Ind AS 2?
o: Storage costs necessary before a further stage of production
Selling and distribution costs incurred in securing the order
General administrative overheads of the corporate office
Abnormal amounts of wasted material, labour and other cost
why: Storage costs are capitalised only where that storage is a necessary part of the production process, such as maturing goods. Abnormal waste, selling costs and general administration are expressly excluded by Ind AS 2.

q: Under SA 501, if the auditor is unable to attend physical inventory counting due to unforeseen circumstances, the auditor should:
o: Immediately issue a qualified opinion on the inventory balance figure
Count on an alternative date and test the intervening transactions
Rely on the management representation about inventory quantities
Accept the internal audit count without performing further work
why: SA 501 requires counting on an alternative date with procedures over intervening movements when attendance is impracticable due to unforeseen circumstances. Modification is required only if no alternative procedures can give sufficient appropriate evidence.

q: A material portion of inventory is held by a third party warehouse. Under SA 501, the auditor primary response is to:
o: Test only the purchase invoices for the goods sent to that warehouse
Take no action, since custody rests with the third party operator
Confirm quantities with the custodian, or attend the count there
Obtain a written representation from the directors on such stock
why: SA 501 requires direct confirmation from the custodian regarding quantities and condition, or attendance at a physical count at that location. Where doubts exist about the custodian integrity or objectivity, further procedures such as inspection or a service auditor report are needed.

q: A company uses weighted average cost. Opening stock 200 units at Rs 90. Purchases: 300 units at Rs 100 then 500 units at Rs 110. Sales during the period: 700 units. Under the periodic weighted average method, the closing inventory value for 300 units is approximately:
o: Rs 33,000 using the latest price
why: Total cost is 18000 plus 30000 plus 55000 equals Rs 1,03,000 for 1000 units, giving a weighted average of Rs 103 per unit and closing inventory of Rs 30,900. Using the latest purchase price of Rs 110 would be FIFO, not weighted average.

q: Ind AS 2 prohibits which of the following cost formulas?
o: Specific identification for items not ordinarily interchangeable
First in first out applied to interchangeable items
Weighted average cost computed on a periodic basis
Last in first out applied to interchangeable items
why: Ind AS 2 permits FIFO and weighted average, and requires specific identification for items that are not ordinarily interchangeable. LIFO is not permitted because it does not reflect a reliable representation of inventory flows.

q: Raw materials held for production have a cost of Rs 10 lakh and a current replacement cost of Rs 8 lakh. The finished goods into which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. Under Ind AS 2 the raw materials should be:
o: Carried at cost of Rs 10 lakh, without any write down
Carried at Rs 9 lakh, the average of cost and replacement
Written down to nil pending sale of the finished goods
Written down to Rs 8 lakh, the current replacement cost
why: Materials are not written down below cost if the finished products in which they will be incorporated are expected to be sold at or above cost. Replacement cost becomes a proxy for NRV only when a decline indicates that the finished goods will sell below cost.

q: While testing inventory cut-off at a year end of 31 March, the auditor finds goods received on 29 March recorded as a purchase on 3 April, but the goods were included in the physical count. The effect on the financial statements before adjustment is:
o: Only a disclosure issue, with no effect on reported amounts
Inventory and profit overstated, liabilities understated
Inventory understated, liabilities overstated, profit understated
No net effect, as inventory and purchases both change equally
why: The goods sit in closing inventory but the corresponding purchase and trade payable are omitted, so cost of sales is understated and profit and inventory are both overstated. The offsetting argument fails because only one side of the transaction was recorded.

q: Which inventory analytic best identifies potential slow-moving or obsolete stock?
o: Recomputing the standard cost per unit for the top ten items
Comparing the gross margin percentage with the prior year
Reviewing ageing by last movement date with turnover by SKU
Reconciling the inventory ledger to the general ledger control
why: Ageing by last movement date combined with SKU level turnover directly identifies items not consumed or sold, which is the substance of obsolescence risk. Gross margin comparison and ledger reconciliations address valuation trends and completeness, not item level slow movement.

q: Under Ind AS 2, a write down of inventory to net realisable value in a prior period is reversed when NRV recovers. The reversal is:
o: Recognised as revenue in the period in which NRV recovers
Prohibited once inventory has been written down to NRV
Credited to other comprehensive income as a revaluation reserve
Limited to the original write down and credited to the expense
why: Ind AS 2 requires reversal limited to the original write down, recognised as a reduction in the amount of inventories recognised as an expense. It never creates a gain above original cost nor is it presented as revenue.

q: A company purchases inventory on deferred settlement terms with payment due after 12 months, at a price of Rs 55 lakh against a cash price of Rs 50 lakh. Under Ind AS 2, the Rs 5 lakh difference is:
o: Recognised as interest expense over the financing period
Charged to inventory and released on sale within cost of sales
Treated as a trade discount, reducing the cost to Rs 45 lakh
Capitalised as part of the cost of the inventory purchased
why: Where an arrangement effectively contains a financing element, the difference between the purchase price for normal credit terms and the amount paid is recognised as interest expense over the period of financing. Capitalising it would overstate inventory cost.

q: During attendance at a physical count, the auditor performs test counts. Which combination provides evidence over both existence and completeness?
o: Selecting items on the floor and tracing them to the count sheets
Selecting items on the count sheets and tracing them to the floor
Selecting both from sheets to floor and from floor to sheets
Recounting the whole warehouse independently of the count team
why: Tracing from sheets to floor tests existence while tracing from floor to sheets tests completeness, so both directions are needed. A single direction leaves one assertion untested regardless of sample size.

q: A construction of a customised item takes 14 months and is held as inventory. The entity is not permitted to capitalise borrowing costs into inventory when:
o: The entity has specific borrowings for the production run
The production period for the item exceeds twelve months
The inventory needs a substantial period to get ready for its sale
The inventory is produced in large quantities and repetitively
why: Ind AS 23 excludes inventories manufactured or otherwise produced in large quantities on a repetitive basis from the definition of a qualifying asset. A one off customised item over a substantial period can qualify.

q: Which statement about the cost of conversion under Ind AS 2 is correct?
o: Variable overheads are allocated on actual use of facilities
Both fixed and variable overheads go on normal capacity always
Variable production overheads are allocated on normal capacity
Fixed production overheads are allocated on actual facility use
why: Ind AS 2 allocates variable production overheads on the basis of actual use of production facilities and fixed production overheads on normal capacity. Reversing the two bases is a common misconception.

q: In periods of unusually high production, Ind AS 2 requires the fixed overhead allocation per unit to be:
o: Charged wholly to profit or loss for that production period
Increased so that all fixed overheads are fully absorbed
Decreased so that inventories are not measured above cost
Kept at the normal capacity rate whatever the output level
why: The amount of fixed overhead allocated to each unit is decreased in periods of abnormally high production so that inventories are not measured above cost. The normal capacity rate is a ceiling not a fixed rate in such periods.

q: The auditor identifies that management has recorded a general provision of 2 percent on all inventory described as an obsolescence reserve, without item level analysis. The most appropriate audit response is:
o: Require the provision to be raised to 5 percent as a norm
Reclassify the provision as a contingent liability note
Accept it as a prudent and appropriately conservative estimate
Challenge it and require item level ageing and NRV evidence
why: Ind AS 2 requires write downs on an item by item basis using NRV evidence, so a blanket percentage lacks support and may create a smoothing reserve. General provisions are not a substitute for specific NRV assessment.

q: Consumable spares that are expected to be used over more than one period and are directly linked to a specific item of plant should be:
o: Recognised as property plant and equipment under Ind AS 16
Charged to profit or loss in the period they are purchased
Recognised as an intangible asset amortised over plant life
Classified as inventory under Ind AS 2 in every situation
why: Major spare parts and standby equipment qualify as PPE when the entity expects to use them during more than one period, particularly if usable only in connection with a specific asset. Routine spares consumed within a period remain inventory.
